mainEntity.name: How much does an Audi A5 2.0 TDI / 35/40 TDI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost depends on the condition of the replacement unit and the specific engine code. Based on verified market data, used engines typically range from £900 to £2,500, while reconditioned units cost between £2,200 and £4,500.

historyTimeline.h2: Audi A5 2.0 TDI / 35/40 TDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the 2.0 TDI was introduced to the Audi A5 range, it quickly became the dominant powertrain, offering a balance of torque, efficiency, and refinement. Over its production run, it evolved from the EA189 unit-injector platform to the highly refined EA288 common-rail diesel, adopting the modern 35 TDI and 40 TDI badging conventions in later years.

milestones.description: CAGB engine code introduced (143hp), establishing the 2.0 TDI baseline for the B8 generation.
CGLB engine code introduced (170hp), featuring updated injection mapping for higher-spec B8 variants.
CNHA engine code introduced (190hp) for the B9 generation, badged as 40 TDI, featuring improved common-rail injection and emissions controls.
DEUA and DETA engine codes introduced (150hp) for the B9 facelift, badged as 35 TDI, integrating refined AdBlue systems and updated EGR cooling for stricter Euro 6d compliance.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Audi A5 2.0 TDI / 35/40 TDI is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Audi A5 2.0 TDI / 35/40 TDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Audi A5 2.0 TDI / 35/40 TDI is generally robust, but specific emissions and cooling components carry known vulnerabilities. The CGLB and CNHA codes dominate replacement demand for this variant due to EGR and DPF-related complexities. Rebuilt engines sourced through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: EGR Cooler & Valve Clogging - Why the Audi A5 2.0 TDI / 35/40 TDI Loses Performance
problems.affectedModels: Audi A5 2.0 TDI / 35/40 TDI (CAGB, CGLB, CNHA, 2007-2020)
problems.rootCause: Carbon buildup from exhaust gas recirculation restricts flow and can cause the EGR cooler to leak coolant into the intake, leading to overheating or hydrolock if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: EGR valve cleaning or replacement, cooler inspection
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early before secondary engine damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt unit with updated EGR components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if coolant ingress has caused cylinder scoring or severe internal damage

problems.recommendation: For older B8 models approaching the lower end of the value spectrum, a verified low-mileage used engine or targeted EGR/DPF repair is often the most economically viable route. For B9 35/40 TDI models, a reconditioned engine is a strong investment, provided the specialist verifies the AdBlue and DPF systems are fully functional to prevent repeat issues.

problems.h4: DPF Blockage & AdBlue System Faults - Why the Audi A5 2.0 TDI / 35/40 TDI Enters Limp Mode
problems.affectedModels: Audi A5 2.0 TDI / 35/40 TDI (CNHA, DEUA, DETA, 2016-present)
problems.rootCause: Frequent short urban journeys prevent active DPF regeneration, while AdBlue heater or NOx sensor failures trigger emissions-related limp mode, restricting engine performance.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: AdBlue sensor/heater replacement and forced DPF regeneration
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if the engine block and turbo remain in good health

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt unit with updated emissions components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if severe DPF blockage has caused turbo contamination or backpressure damage
